title.zh: 卷一百三十七 列傳第二十四: 察罕 曲樞 阿禮海牙 奕赫抵雅爾丁 脫烈海牙
title.en: Volume 137 Biographies 24: Chahan, Qushu, Alihaiya, Yihediyaerding, Tuoliehaiya
title.raw: 卷一百三十七 列傳第二十四: 察罕 曲樞 阿禮海牙 奕赫抵雅爾丁 脫烈海牙 Volume 137 Biographies 24: Chahan, Qushu, Alihaiya, Yihediyaerding, Tuoliehaiya

sentences.zh: 察罕，西域板勒紇城人也。

translations.literal: Chahan was a man of Banshilahe city in the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Chahan was a native of Banshilahe in the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 父伯德那，歲庚辰，國兵下西域，舉族來歸。

translations.literal: His father Berdena—in the gengchen year, when the imperial army descended upon the Western Regions, brought the whole clan to submit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Berdena had led the entire clan over in submission when the imperial armies swept the Western Regions in the gengchen year (1220).

sentences.zh: 事親王旭烈，授河東民賦副緫管，因居河中猗氏縣，後徙解州。

translations.literal: He served Prince Xulie and was appointed deputy chief commissioner for the civilian tax levy in Hedong; he therefore resided in Yishi county in Hezhong, and later moved to Jie prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Prince Xulie, he received appointment as deputy chief commissioner of the Hedong civilian tax levy; his household settled in Yishi county in Hezhong and later moved to Jie prefecture.

sentences.zh: 贈榮祿大夫、宣徽使、柱國、芮國公。

translations.literal: [Posthumously] conferred: Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, Pillar of the State, Duke of Rui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, made a Pillar of the State, and created Duke of Rui.

sentences.zh: 察罕魁偉穎悟，博覽強記，通諸國字書，為行軍府奧魯千戶。

translations.literal: Chahan was tall and imposing, quick-witted, widely read with a strong memory; he mastered the scripts of various countries and served as chiliarch of the ordu of the campaigning army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Chahan was imposing in stature and sharp of mind, a wide reader with a formidable memory who mastered the written languages of many realms; he held the post of chiliarch of the campaigning army's ordu.

sentences.zh: 奧魯赤參政湖廣，辟為蒙古都萬戶府知事。

translations.literal: When Oljei became regional councilor of Huguang, he recruited him as director of affairs in the Mongol Chief Ten-Thousand Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Oljei took up office as Huguang regional councilor, he recruited Chahan as director of affairs in the Mongol Chief Ten-Thousand Households Office.

sentences.zh: 奧魯赤進平章，復辟為理問，政事悉委裁決，且令諸子受學焉。

translations.literal: When Oljei was promoted to Grand Councillor, he again recruited him as judicial intendant; he entrusted all administrative decisions to his judgment and had his sons study under him as well.
translations.idiomatic: After Oljei advanced to grand councillor, he again brought Chahan in as judicial intendant, leaving the full weight of administrative decisions to his judgment and setting his own sons to study under him.

sentences.zh: 至元二十四年，從鎮南王征安南，師次瀘江。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan (1287), he followed the Prince of Zhennan on the campaign against Annam; the army halted at the Lu River.
translations.idiomatic: In 1287 he followed the Prince of Zhennan against Annam, the expedition halting at the Lu River.

sentences.zh: 安南世子遣其叔父詣軍門自陳無罪，王命察罕數其罪而責之，使者辭屈，世子舉衆逃去。

translations.literal: The crown prince of Annam sent his paternal uncle to the camp gate to declare their innocence; the prince ordered Chahan to enumerate their crimes and rebuke them; the envoy could not answer, and the crown prince fled with his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Annam's heir sent his uncle to the camp to plead their innocence; the prince ordered Chahan to itemize their offenses and rebuke them. When the envoy could find no reply, the heir broke camp and fled with his troops.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授樞密院經歷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year (1291), he was appointed secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1291 he was appointed secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾從奧魯赤移治江西。

translations.literal: Before long he followed Oljei when the latter's administration moved to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he accompanied Oljei when his administration was transferred to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 寧都民言：「某鄉石上雲氣五色，有物焉，視之玉璽也。

translations.literal: The people of Ningdu said: "In a certain village, five-colored clouds rise from a stone, and there is something on it that, when looked at, appears to be a jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: People in Ningdu reported: "In one village, five-colored vapors hover over a stone, and something on it looks, upon inspection, like a jade imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 不以兵取，恐為居人所有。」

translations.literal: If troops are not sent to take it, I fear the local residents will possess it."
translations.idiomatic: Unless troops are sent to seize it, the locals may claim it for themselves."

sentences.zh: 衆惑之。

translations.literal: The crowd was disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: The populace was thrown into confusion.

sentences.zh: 察罕曰：「妄也，是必搆害仇家者。」

translations.literal: Chahan said: "This is nonsense; it must be someone framing a rival family."
translations.idiomatic: Chahan said: "This is sheer fabrication—someone is surely framing a rival household."

sentences.zh: 覈問之果然。

translations.literal: Upon investigation it proved to be so.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation confirmed it at once.

sentences.zh: 前後從奧魯赤出入湖廣、江西兩省，凡二十一年，多著勳績。

translations.literal: In all he followed Oljei in and out of the two provinces of Huguang and Jiangxi for twenty-one years, achieving many meritorious deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Over twenty-one years he followed Oljei between Huguang and Jiangxi, compiling a long record of distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德四年，御史臺奏僉湖南憲司事，中書省奏為武昌路治中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade under Emperor Chengzong (1300), the Censorate memorialized to appoint him to the Hunan surveillance commission; the Central Secretariat memorialized to make him administrative vice-commissioner of Wuchang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1300 the Censorate recommended him for the Hunan surveillance commission, while the Central Secretariat proposed him as administrative vice-commissioner of Wuchang circuit.

sentences.zh: 丞相哈剌哈孫曰：「察罕廉潔，固宜居風憲。

translations.literal: The Chief Councillor Harqasun said: "Chahan is incorrupt; he is indeed fit for censorial office.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Harqasun said: "Chahan is incorruptible and well suited to censorial duty.

sentences.zh: 然武昌大郡，非斯人不可治。」

translations.literal: Yet Wuchang is a great commandery; no one but this man can govern it."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wuchang is a great commandery—no one but he can govern it properly."

sentences.zh: 竟除武昌。

translations.literal: In the end he was appointed to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was appointed to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 廣西妖賊高仙道以左道惑衆，平民詿誤者以數千計。

translations.literal: The sorcerer-rebel Gao Xiandao of Guangxi used heterodox teachings to delude the masses; commoners misled into involvement numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxi the sorcerer-rebel Gao Xiandao led crowds astray with heterodox teachings, and thousands of commoners were drawn in through deception.

sentences.zh: 既敗，湖廣行省命察罕與憲司雜治之，鞫得其情，議誅首惡數人，餘悉縱遣，且焚其籍。

translations.literal: After their defeat, the Huguang Branch Secretariat ordered Chahan and the surveillance commission to try the cases jointly; the inquiry established the facts, and it was proposed to execute several ringleaders while releasing all the rest and burning their registers.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, the Huguang Branch Secretariat ordered Chahan and the surveillance officials to try the cases together. Once the facts were established, he proposed executing only the chief culprits, releasing everyone else, and burning the registers.

sentences.zh: 衆難之。

translations.literal: The others objected.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues objected.

sentences.zh: 察罕曰：「吾獨當其責，諸君無累也。」

translations.literal: Chahan said: "I alone will bear the responsibility; you gentlemen need not be implicated."
translations.idiomatic: Chahan said: "I alone will answer for this—none of you need fear repercussions."

sentences.zh: 以治最聞，擢河南省郎中。

translations.literal: His governance became renowned as the finest, and he was promoted to director in the Henan Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His administration won the highest repute, and he was promoted to director in the Henan Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，仁宗自藩邸入誅群臣之為異謀者，迎武宗于邊。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Renzong entered from his princely residence to execute the ministers who had plotted treason, and welcomed Wuzong from the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, Renzong left his princely residence to execute ministers implicated in treasonous designs and went to the frontier to welcome Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 河南平章囊加台薦察罕，即驛召至上都，賜廄馬二匹、鈔一千貫、銀五十兩，曰：「卿少留，行用卿矣。」

translations.literal: Nangatai, Grand Councillor of Henan, recommended Chahan; he was summoned by post-haste relay to Shangdu and granted two stable horses, a thousand strings of paper money, and fifty taels of silver, with the words: "Stay a little longer—you will soon be put to use."
translations.idiomatic: Nangatai, grand councillor of Henan, recommended Chahan, who was summoned by urgent relay to Shangdu and given two stable horses, a thousand strings of paper money, and fifty taels of silver, with the message: "Remain a while longer—I shall soon put you to work."

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，立仁宗為皇太子，授察罕詹事院判，進僉詹事院事，賜銀百兩、錦二匹。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne he installed Renzong as crown prince, appointed Chahan vice-director of the Household of the Heir Apparent, then promoted him to associate director of the Household of the Heir Apparent, and granted him a hundred taels of silver and two lengths of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended the throne he named Renzong crown prince, appointed Chahan vice-director of the Household of the Heir Apparent, then promoted him to associate director of that office, and granted him a hundred taels of silver and two lengths of brocade.

sentences.zh: 遣先還大都立院事。

translations.literal: He was sent back first to Dadu to establish the affairs of the household.
translations.idiomatic: Chahan was sent ahead to Dadu to set the household administration in order.

sentences.zh: 仁宗至，謂曰：「上以故安西王地賜我，置都緫管府，卿其領之，慎揀僚屬，勿以詹事位高不屑此也。

translations.literal: When Renzong arrived he said to him: "The emperor has granted me the former lands of the Prince of Anxi and established a metropolitan chief commissioner's office; you are to head it. Choose your subordinates carefully, and do not disdain this post because your rank as director of the heir's household is high.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong arrived he told him: "The emperor has granted me the former Anxi princely domains and established a metropolitan chief commissioner's office—take charge of it. Choose your staff with care, and do not scorn the post because your rank in the heir's household is lofty.

sentences.zh: 進卿秩資德大夫。」

translations.literal: I advance your rank to Grand Master of Virtuous Merit."
translations.idiomatic: I shall advance your rank to Grand Master of Virtuous Merit."

sentences.zh: 察罕叩頭謝曰：「都府之職，敢不恭命，進秩非所敢當。」

translations.literal: Chahan kowtowed in thanks and said: "The metropolitan office—I dare not fail to obey your command; the promotion in rank is more than I dare accept."
translations.idiomatic: Chahan kowtowed and replied: "The metropolitan office—I dare not refuse your command; but the promotion in rank is more than I may accept."

sentences.zh: 固辭，改正奉大夫，授以銀印。

translations.literal: He firmly declined, and his rank was changed to Grand Master of Proper Service; he was granted a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined, and his rank was set at Grand Master of Proper Service instead, with a silver seal conferred upon him.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，閱戶口江南諸省，還進太子府正，加昭文館大學士，遷家令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida (1308), he reviewed household registers in the Jiangnan provinces; on his return he was promoted to Director of the Heir Apparent's Household, advanced to Grand Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Literature, and transferred to Master of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he reviewed household registers across the Jiangnan provinces. On his return he was promoted to director of the heir's household, granted the title Grand Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Literature, and made master of the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 武宗崩，仁宗哀慟不已。

translations.literal: When Wuzong died, Renzong grieved and mourned unceasingly.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong died, Renzong grieved without cease.

sentences.zh: 察罕再拜啟曰：「庶民修短，尚云有數，聖人天命，夫豈偶然？

translations.literal: Chahan bowed twice and addressed him, saying: "The length of a commoner's life is said to have its allotted span; the mandate of a sage is Heaven's will—how could it be mere chance?
translations.idiomatic: Chahan bowed twice and addressed him: "Even commoners' allotted spans are said to be fixed; how much less could a sage's mandate be mere chance?

sentences.zh: 天下重器懸於殿下，縱自苦，如宗廟、太后何？」

translations.literal: The great vessel of the realm hangs upon Your Highness; even if you afflict yourself, what of the ancestral temples and the empress dowager?"
translations.idiomatic: The great charge of empire rests upon Your Highness; if you afflict yourself, what becomes of the ancestral temples and the empress dowager?"

sentences.zh: 仁宗輟泣曰：「曩者大喪必命浮屠，何益？

translations.literal: Renzong checked his weeping and said: "In past great mourning Buddhist monks were always summoned—of what use was it?
translations.idiomatic: Renzong restrained his tears and said: "At past imperial funerals Buddhist monks were always summoned—what good did it do?

sentences.zh: 吾欲發府庫以賑鰥寡孤獨，若何？」

translations.literal: I wish to open the treasury to relieve widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish to open the treasury to relieve widowers, widows, orphans, and the helpless—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「發政施仁，文王所以為聖。

translations.literal: He said: "Issuing benevolent policies and dispensing kindness—this is why King Wen became a sage.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Issuing benevolent policies and extending kindness—this is why King Wen became a sage.

sentences.zh: 殿下行之幸甚。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness carries it out, it would be most fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness does the same, it would be a great blessing."

sentences.zh: 東宮故有左右衞兵，命囊加台、察罕總右衞，且令審擇官屬。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace had long had left and right guard troops; he ordered Nangatai and Chahan to command the Right Guard, and also directed them to scrutinize and select officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace already had left and right guard troops. Renzong ordered Nangatai and Chahan to command the Right Guard and directed them to select their staff with care.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，拜中書參知政事，但緫持綱維，不屑細務，識者謂得大臣體。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, Chahan was appointed Associate Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat; he held only to the great principles and disdained petty affairs, and those who understood such things said he had the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong ascended the throne, Chahan was made associate grand councillor of the Central Secretariat. He held to the broad outlines of policy and disdained petty detail, and observers said he had the bearing of a true statesman.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗賜枸杞酒，曰：「以益卿壽。」

translations.literal: The emperor once bestowed wolfberry wine upon him, saying: "To prolong your life."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once gave him wolfberry wine, saying: "To add years to your life."

sentences.zh: 又語宰相曰：「察罕清素，可賜金束帶、鈔萬貫。」

translations.literal: He also told the chief ministers: "Chahan is plain and incorrupt; grant him a gold belt and ten thousand strings of paper money."
translations.idiomatic: He also told the chief ministers: "Chahan lives plainly and without corruption—grant him a gold belt and ten thousand strings of paper money."

sentences.zh: 前後賞賚不可勝計。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards bestowed upon him before and after were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，進榮祿大夫、平章政事、商議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing (1312), he was advanced to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Grand Councillor, and Commissioner for Deliberation on Central Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1312 he was promoted to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, grand councillor, and commissioner for deliberation on Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 乞歸解州立碑先塋，許之。

translations.literal: He requested leave to return to Jie prefecture to erect a stele at his ancestors' tomb; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to return to Jie prefecture and set up a stele at his family's burial ground; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 暮年，居德安白雲山別墅，以白雲自號。

translations.literal: In his later years he resided at a villa on White Cloud Mountain in De'an and took White Cloud as his sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he lived at a villa on White Cloud Mountain in De'an and styled himself Master White Cloud.

sentences.zh: 嘗入見，帝望見曰：「白雲先生來也。」

translations.literal: Once when he came to audience, the emperor saw him from afar and said: "Master White Cloud has come."
translations.idiomatic: Once when he came to audience, the emperor caught sight of him and said: "Master White Cloud has arrived."

sentences.zh: 其被寵遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the degree of favor he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問張良何如人，對曰：「佐高帝，興漢，功成身退，賢者也。」

translations.literal: The emperor once asked what sort of man Zhang Liang was; he replied: "He assisted the High Emperor, raised Han, and withdrew when his work was done—a man of worth."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked what manner of man Zhang Liang had been; he answered: "He aided the High Emperor, raised Han to power, and withdrew once his work was done—a man of true merit."

sentences.zh: 又問狄仁傑，對曰：「當唐室中衰，能卒保社稷，亦賢相也。」

translations.literal: He was asked about Di Renjie and replied: "When the Tang house was in mid-decline, he was able in the end to preserve the altars of state—he too was a worthy minister."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Di Renjie, he replied: "When the Tang house was in decline, he was able in the end to preserve the realm—another worthy minister."

sentences.zh: 因誦范仲淹所撰碑詞甚熟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recited from memory the stele inscription composed by Fan Zhongyan with great fluency.
translations.idiomatic: He then recited from memory, with great fluency, the stele inscription Fan Zhongyan had composed.

sentences.zh: 帝歎息良久曰：「察罕博學如此邪。」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed for a long while and said: "Chahan is so learned as this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed at length and said: "Chahan's learning runs this deep!"

sentences.zh: 嘗譯貞觀政要以獻。

translations.literal: He once translated the Essentials of Government in the Zhenguan Reign and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He once translated the Essentials of Government in the Zhenguan Reign and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，詔繕寫遍賜左右。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered it copied and distributed widely to those around him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and ordered copies made and distributed throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 且詔譯帝範。

translations.literal: He also ordered the translation of the Models for Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Models for Emperors to be translated.

sentences.zh: 又命譯脫必赤顏名曰聖武開天紀，及紀年纂要、太宗平金始末等書，俱付史館。

translations.literal: He further ordered the translation of the Tobchiyan, entitled Records of the Sagely Martial Opening of Heaven, as well as the Compendium of Chronology, the Complete Account of Taizong's Pacification of Jin, and other books, all of which were delivered to the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He further ordered the translation of the Tobchiyan under the title Records of the Sagely Martial Opening of Heaven, along with the Compendium of Chronology, the Complete Account of Taizong's Pacification of Jin, and other works, all of which were deposited in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 嘗以病請告，暨還朝，帝御萬歲山圓殿，與平章李孟入謝。

translations.literal: Once he requested leave on grounds of illness; when he returned to court, the emperor held audience in the round hall on Longevity Mountain, and he entered with Grand Councillor Li Meng to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Once, after requesting sick leave, he returned to court; the emperor received audience in the round hall on Longevity Mountain, and Chahan entered with Grand Councillor Li Meng to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「白雲病愈邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Has Master White Cloud recovered from his illness?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Has Master White Cloud recovered?"

sentences.zh: 頓首對曰：「老臣衰病，無補聖明，荷陛下哀矜，放歸田里，幸甚，不覺沉痾去體爾。」

translations.literal: He kowtowed and replied: "This old minister's declining illness is of no benefit to your sagely clarity; I am deeply obliged that Your Majesty in compassion released me to the countryside—how fortunate—and I did not notice my grave malady leaving my body."
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed and answered: "Your old servant's failing health can no longer serve your enlightened rule. I am deeply grateful that Your Majesty in compassion released me to the countryside—so fortunate am I that my lingering illness has left me without my noticing."

sentences.zh: 命賜茵以坐。

translations.literal: He was ordered to be given a cushion and seated.
translations.idiomatic: He was told to sit on a cushion provided for him.

sentences.zh: 顧李孟曰：「知止不辱，今見其人。

translations.literal: Turning to Li Meng he said: "To know when to stop and avoid disgrace—today I see such a man.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Li Meng he said: "To know when to stop and so avoid disgrace—today I see such a man.

sentences.zh: 朕始以荅剌罕、不憐吉台、囊加台等言用之，誠多裨益。

translations.literal: At first I employed him on the advice of Darqan, Bolinjigai, Nangatai, and others, and he truly brought great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: At first I put him to use on the advice of Darqan, Bolinjigai, Nangatai, and others, and he has indeed been of great benefit.

sentences.zh: 有言察罕不善者，其人即非善人也。」

translations.literal: Whoever speaks ill of Chahan is himself no good man."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever speaks ill of Chahan is no good man himself."

sentences.zh: 又語及科舉并前古帝王賜姓命氏之事，因賜察罕姓白氏。

translations.literal: He also spoke of the civil examinations and of how ancient emperors bestowed surnames and clans, and on that account granted Chahan the surname Bai.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of the civil examinations and of how ancient emperors bestowed surnames and clan names, and on that account granted Chahan the surname Bai.

sentences.zh: 初，察罕生於河中，其夜，天氣清肅，月白如晝。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chahan was born in Hezhong, that night the weather was clear and still, and the moon was white as daylight.
translations.idiomatic: When Chahan was born in Hezhong, the night was clear and still, and the moon shone white as day.

sentences.zh: 相者賀曰：「是兒必貴。」

translations.literal: A physiognomist congratulated them, saying: "This child will surely rise to eminence."
translations.idiomatic: A physiognomist offered congratulations: "This child is destined for greatness."

sentences.zh: 國人謂白為察罕，故名察罕。

translations.literal: Among his people "white" is called chahan, and so he was named Chahan.
translations.idiomatic: In their tongue "white" is chahan, and so he was given the name Chahan.

sentences.zh: 察罕天性孝友，田宅之在河中者，悉分與諸昆弟。

translations.literal: Chahan was filial and fraternal by nature; the fields and houses he held in Hezhong he divided entirely among his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Chahan was filial and brotherly; he divided all his fields and houses in Hezhong among his brothers.

sentences.zh: 昆弟貧來歸者，復分與田宅奴婢，縱奴為民者甚衆。

translations.literal: When brothers returned in poverty he again divided fields, houses, and slaves among them, and the number of slaves he freed to become commoners was very great.
translations.idiomatic: When brothers came home in poverty he again shared out land, houses, and bondsmen, and he freed a great many slaves to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 故人多稱長者。

translations.literal: Therefore many called him a man of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason many called him a man of true stature.

sentences.zh: 既致仕，優游八年，以壽終。

translations.literal: After he retired from office he lived at ease for eight years and died at a full age.
translations.idiomatic: After retirement he lived at ease for eight years and died at a full age.

sentences.zh: 子外家奴，太中大夫、武岡路緫管；

translations.literal: His son Waijianu was Grand Master of the Palace, chief commissioner of Wugang circuit;
translations.idiomatic: His son Waijianu served as Grand Master of the Palace and chief commissioner of Wugang circuit;

sentences.zh: 李家奴，早卒；

translations.literal: Lijianu died young;
translations.idiomatic: Lijianu died young;

sentences.zh: 忽都篤，承直郎、高郵府判官。

translations.literal: Hutudu was Gentleman for Upholding Integrity and assistant prefect of Gaoyou prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hutudu held the rank of Gentleman for Upholding Integrity and served as assistant prefect of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 孫九人，仕者二人：闊闊不花、哈撒。

translations.literal: He had nine grandsons; two entered office: Kuokuobuhua and Hasa.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine grandsons, of whom two held office: Kuokuobuhua and Hasa.

sentences.zh: 曲樞，西土人。

translations.literal: Qushu was a man of the Western Lands.
translations.idiomatic: Qushu was a native of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 曾祖達不台，祖阿達台，父質理花台，世贈功臣，追封王爵。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Tabutai, his grandfather Adatai, his father Zhilihuatai; generation after generation they were posthumously enfeoffed as meritorious ministers and granted princely titles.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Tabutai, his grandfather Adatai, and his father Zhilihuatai; for generations the family received posthumous honors as meritorious ministers and princely enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 曲樞七歲失怙恃。

translations.literal: Qushu lost both parents at the age of seven.
translations.idiomatic: Qushu lost both parents when he was seven.

sentences.zh: 既壯，沉密靜專，為徽仁裕聖皇太后宮臣。

translations.literal: When he reached maturity he was deep, reserved, quiet, and single-minded, and became a palace attendant to the Empress Dowager of Sagely Benevolence and Abundant Sagacity.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was grave, reserved, and steadfast, and entered service as a palace attendant to the Empress Dowager of Sagely Benevolence and Abundant Sagacity.

sentences.zh: 仁宗幼時，以曲樞可任保傅，左右擁翼。

translations.literal: When Renzong was young, Qushu was judged fit to serve as guardian and tutor, and attended him on either side.
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong's youth Qushu was judged fit to serve as guardian and tutor and attended him closely on either hand.

sentences.zh: 曲樞入則佐視食飲，出則抱負游衍，鞠躬盡力，夙夜匪懈。

translations.literal: Qushu within assisted in overseeing food and drink; without he carried and supported him in his wanderings and play, bowing with all his strength and never slackening morning or night.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace Qushu helped oversee his meals; outside he carried and guided him in his walks and play, bending every effort and never slackening day or night.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，武宗緫戎北邊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade (1299), Wuzong commanded the armies on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In 1299 Wuzong took command of the northern armies.

sentences.zh: 九年，讒人亂國。

translations.literal: In the ninth year (1305), slanderers threw the state into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In 1305 slanderers threw the state into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 仁宗侍皇太后之國于懷，未幾，復之雲中，連年奔走不暇。

translations.literal: Renzong attended the empress dowager when she went to her fief in Huai; before long they returned to Yunzhong, and for years on end they were constantly on the move without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong accompanied the empress dowager to her fief in Huai; before long they were back in Yunzhong, and for years they were constantly on the move without respite.

sentences.zh: 曲樞櫛風沐雨，跋涉艱險，無倦色。

translations.literal: Qushu braved wind and rain, traversed hardships and dangers, and showed no sign of weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Qushu braved wind and rain, crossed difficult terrain, and never showed weariness.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，仁宗奉太后入朝，殲姦黨，迎武宗即皇帝位，仁宗為皇太子，天下以安。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Renzong escorted the empress dowager to court, destroyed the faction of traitors, welcomed Wuzong to the imperial throne, and installed Renzong as crown prince; the realm was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, Renzong brought the empress dowager to court, destroyed the treacherous faction, and welcomed Wuzong to the throne while Renzong was named crown prince; the realm was thereby settled.

sentences.zh: 拜曲樞榮祿大夫、平章政事，行大司農。

translations.literal: Qushu was appointed Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and Grand Councillor, acting as Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Qushu was appointed Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and grand councillor, with acting charge of the Ministry of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進光祿大夫，領詹事院事，加特進，封應國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, put in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent, given the special advancement rank, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, placed in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent, granted special advancement, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，拜開府儀同三司、太子詹事、平章軍國重事、上柱國，依前大司農、應國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida (1308) he was granted the rank of Kaifu Yitong Sansi, with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies, and appointed Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and Grand Councillor for Military and State Affairs of the First Rank; he was also made a Pillar of the State while retaining his former posts as Minister of Agriculture and Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he was granted the rank of Kaifu Yitong Sansi (with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies), appointed Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and grand councillor for military and state affairs of the first rank, made a Pillar of the State, and retained as Minister of Agriculture and Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 進太子太保，領典醫監事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and put in charge of the Imperial Medical Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and placed in charge of the Imperial Medical Service.

sentences.zh: 四年，授太保、錄軍國重事、集賢大學士，兼大司農，領崇祥院、司天臺事，官爵勳封如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year (1311) he was appointed Grand Guardian, Recorder of Military and State Affairs of the First Rank, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, while also serving as Minister of Agriculture and overseeing the Chongxiang Court and the Directorate of Astronomy; his offices, titles, honors, and enfeoffment remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 1311 he was appointed Grand Guardian, recorder of military and state affairs of the first rank, and grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, while continuing as Minister of Agriculture and overseeing the Chongxiang Court and the Directorate of Astronomy; his other offices, honors, and enfeoffment were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 後以疾薨于位。

translations.literal: Later he died in office of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in office of illness.

sentences.zh: 子二人。

translations.literal: He had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons.

sentences.zh: 長伯都，大德十一年特授翰林學士、嘉議大夫，遷中奉大夫、典寶監卿，加資德大夫、治書侍御史。

translations.literal: The elder, Bodu, was specially appointed in the eleventh year of Dade (1307) as Hanlin Academician and Grand Master of Court Discussion, then transferred to Grand Master of Proper Service and Director of the Imperial Treasuries, and further advanced to Grand Master of Virtuous Merit and Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The elder son Bodu was specially appointed in 1307 as Hanlin academician and Grand Master of Court Discussion, then promoted to Grand Master of Proper Service and director of the Imperial Treasuries, and further advanced to Grand Master of Virtuous Merit and investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，陞榮祿大夫，遙授中書平章政事，改侍御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida (1308) he was raised to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, given the honorary appointment of Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat, and transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he was raised to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, given the honorary title of grand councillor of the Central Secretariat, and transferred to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜中書參知政事，進右丞，年三十二而卒。

translations.literal: The following year he was appointed Associate Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat and advanced to Right Vice Councillor; he died at the age of thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made associate grand councillor of the Central Secretariat and promoted to right vice councillor; he died at thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 子咬住。

translations.literal: His son was Yaozhu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yaozhu.

sentences.zh: 次伯帖木兒，大德十一年，特授正議大夫、懷孟路總管府達魯花赤，兼管諸軍奧魯管內勸農事，改府正。

translations.literal: The younger, Botemuer, was specially appointed in the eleventh year of Dade (1307) as Grand Master of Proper Discussion and darughachi of the Huaimeng Route Chief Commissioner's Office, concurrently overseeing agricultural affairs within the ordu under the various armies, then transferred to Prefect of the Office.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son Botemuer was specially appointed in 1307 as Grand Master of Proper Discussion and darughachi of the Huaimeng Route chief commissioner's office, overseeing agricultural affairs within the armies' ordus, and was later made prefect of the office.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，遷中奉大夫、陝西等處行尚書省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida (1309) he was transferred to Grand Master of Proper Service and Associate Grand Councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309 he was transferred to Grand Master of Proper Service and associate grand councillor of the Shaanxi branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，入為太子家令，遷正奉大夫。

translations.literal: The following year he entered service as Master of the Heir Apparent's Household and was advanced to Grand Master for Proper Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he entered service as master of the heir's household and was advanced to Grand Master for Proper Attendance.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷資德大夫、大都留守，兼少府監。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to Grand Master of Virtuous Merit, Metropolitan Intendant, and concurrently Director of the Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Grand Master of Virtuous Merit, metropolitan intendant, and concurrently director of the Imperial Workshops.

sentences.zh: 擬擢侍御史，改除翰林學士承旨、知制誥兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was slated for promotion to Attending Censor but was instead appointed Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, Director of Imperial Edicts, and Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was slated for promotion to attending censor but was instead appointed chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, director of imperial edicts, and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 未幾復為大都留守，兼少府監、武衞親軍都指揮使，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made Metropolitan Intendant, concurrently Director of the Imperial Workshops and Chief Commander of the Wuwei Guard Princely Army, and wore the gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again made metropolitan intendant, concurrently director of the Imperial Workshops and chief commander of the Wuwei Guard princely army, and was granted the gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，加榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing (1312) he was advanced to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1312 he was advanced to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子二人：桓澤都，蠻子。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Huanzedu and Manzi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Huanzedu and Manzi.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙

translations.literal: Alihaiya
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙，畏吾氏，集賢大學士脫列之子也。

translations.literal: Alihaiya was of the Uyghur clan; he was the son of Tuolie, Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya was of Uyghur descent, the son of Tuolie, grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 兄野訥，事仁宗於潛邸。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yene had served Renzong at his hidden residence.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yene had served Renzong when he was still heir in waiting.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，仁宗奉興聖太后出居懷州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dade (1305), Renzong escorted the Empress Dowager of Sagely Birth out to reside in Huai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1305 Renzong escorted the Empress Dowager of Sagely Birth to take up residence in Huai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從者單弱，多懷去計。

translations.literal: The followers were few and weak, and many harbored plans to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Their following was thin, and many among them thought of leaving.

sentences.zh: 野訥獨無所畏難。

translations.literal: Yene alone showed no fear or difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Yene alone showed no fear or hesitation.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，權臣阿附中宮，不遣使告哀宗藩。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, powerful ministers attached themselves to the empress's palace and did not send envoys to announce the mourning to the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, powerful ministers curried favor with the empress's palace and sent no envoys to announce the mourning to the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 仁宗有聞，將自懷州入京，宮臣或持不可。

translations.literal: When word reached Renzong, he prepared to enter the capital from Huai prefecture, but some palace attendants held that this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached Renzong, he prepared to enter the capital from Huai, but some palace attendants argued against it.

sentences.zh: 野訥屏人密啟曰：「天子晏駕而皇子已早卒，天下無主，邪謀方興。

translations.literal: Yene dismissed attendants and secretly reported, saying: "The Son of Heaven has passed away and the imperial prince died early; the realm has no master, and wicked plots are rising.
translations.idiomatic: Yene sent away his attendants and reported in secret: "The emperor is dead and the heir died long ago; the realm has no ruler, and treacherous schemes are already stirring.

sentences.zh: 懷寧王及殿下，世祖、裕皇賢孫，人心所屬久矣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Huaining and Your Highness are worthy descendants of Shizu and Emperor Yuzong; the hearts of the people have long belonged to you.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Huaining and Your Highness are worthy grandsons of Kublai and the Renowned Emperor; the people's loyalty has long rested with you.

sentences.zh: 宜急奉太母入定大計，邪謀必止。

translations.literal: You should swiftly escort the Grand Empress Dowager to settle the great plan; the wicked plots will surely cease.
translations.idiomatic: You should hurry to bring the Grand Empress Dowager and settle the succession; the treacherous schemes will then collapse.

sentences.zh: 迎立懷寧王以正神器，在此行矣。」

translations.literal: To welcome and install the Prince of Huaining to set right the imperial regalia depends on this journey."
translations.idiomatic: Whether the throne can be set right by welcoming and enthroning the Prince of Huaining depends on what you do now."

sentences.zh: 仁宗即白太后，以二月至京師，遂誅柄臣二人，遣使迎武宗。

translations.literal: Renzong immediately informed the empress dowager, and in the second month arrived at the capital, then executed two power-holding ministers and dispatched envoys to welcome Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong at once reported to the empress dowager, reached the capital in the second month, executed two powerful ministers, and sent envoys to welcome Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，召野訥，賜玉帶，授嘉議大夫、祕書監。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended the throne, he summoned Yene, bestowed a jade belt, and appointed him Grand Master of Court Discussion and Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong took the throne, he summoned Yene, granted him a jade belt, and appointed him Grand Master of Court Discussion and director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仁宗居東宮，兼太子右庶子，遷侍御史、崇祥院使，兼將作院使。

translations.literal: While Renzong resided in the Eastern Palace, Yene also served as Right Vice Tutor to the Heir Apparent; he was transferred to Attending Censor, Commissioner of the Chongxiang Court, and concurrently Commissioner of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: While Renzong was crown prince, Yene also served as right vice tutor to the heir apparent; he was later made attending censor and commissioner of the Chongxiang Court, with concurrent charge of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 閩有綉工，工官大集民間子女居肆督責，吏因為奸利，野訥奏罷之，閩人感悅。

translations.literal: In Min there were embroidery artisans; the craft officials greatly gathered the sons and daughters of common families to dwell in workshops under supervision and coercion, and the clerks thereby made illicit profit. Yene memorialized to abolish this, and the people of Min were grateful and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In Fujian, craft officials had rounded up commoners' sons and daughters into supervised embroidery shops, and clerks profited from the abuse. Yene memorialized to abolish the practice, and the people of Min were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 尋兼太醫院使。

translations.literal: Before long he also served as Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added the concurrent post of commissioner of the Imperial Medical Institute.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，請召文武老臣，咨以朝政。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended the throne, Yene requested that veteran civil and military officials be summoned and consulted on court governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, Yene asked that veteran civil and military officials be summoned to advise on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 又請以中都苑囿還諸民。

translations.literal: He also requested that the parks and preserves of the central capital be returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the parks and hunting grounds around the capital be returned to the people.

sentences.zh: 拜樞密院副使，進同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and advanced to Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and promoted to associate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 命為中書平章政事，辭不拜。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat, but declined and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as grand councillor of the Central Secretariat, but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 野訥之在臺及侍禁中，於國家事有不便，輒言之，言無不納。

translations.literal: While Yene served at the Censorate and attended within the forbidden precincts, whenever there was something inconvenient to state affairs he spoke of it, and his words were never rejected.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at the Censorate and in attendance within the palace, Yene spoke out whenever he saw something harmful to the state, and his advice was always accepted.

sentences.zh: 然韜晦惡盈，不泄於外。

translations.literal: Yet he kept himself restrained and hated excess, and did not reveal it outside.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he kept a low profile, shunned self-importance, and disclosed nothing outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 延祐四年卒，年四十。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanyou (1317) he died, at the age of forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1317, at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 贈推誠保節翊運功臣、金紫光祿大夫、行中書省左丞相、上柱國、趙國公，諡忠靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously conferred the title Meritorious Subject Who Sincerely Upholds Integrity and Supports the Dynasty, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Acting Left Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as a meritorious subject who sincerely upheld integrity and supported the dynasty, made Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, acting left grand councillor of the Central Secretariat, a Pillar of the State, and Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Loyal and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙亦早事武宗、仁宗，為宿衛，以清慎通敏與父兄並見信任。

translations.literal: Alihaiya also early served Wuzong and Renzong as a palace guard, and because of his purity, caution, broad competence, and quick intelligence he, together with his father and elder brother, was trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya had also entered the service of Wuzong and Renzong early on as a palace guard; for his integrity, prudence, and quick intelligence, he was trusted along with his father and elder brother.

sentences.zh: 十餘年間，歷華近，入侍帷幄，出踐省闥，廷無間言。

translations.literal: Over more than ten years he rose through lofty posts close to the throne, attending within the imperial curtains when inside and treading the gates of the Secretariat when outside; at court there was no discordant speech.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than ten years he rose through lofty posts close to the throne, serving within the imperial curtains and carrying out duties at the Secretariat gates; at court no one spoke against him.

sentences.zh: 至治初，出為平章政事，歷鎮江浙、湖廣、河南、陝西四省，皆有惠政，汴人尤懷思之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhizhi era (1321) he went out as Grand Councillor and successively governed the four provinces of Jiang-Zhe, Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi; in each he had benevolent policies, and the people of Bian especially cherished and remembered him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhizhi era he was sent out as grand councillor and successively governed Jiang-Zhe, Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi; everywhere he left benevolent rule, and the people of Bian remembered him with special affection.

sentences.zh: 歸朝拜翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Upon returning to court he was appointed Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed chief academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，解官家居。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he resigned his office and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he resigned his office and retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年秋，文宗入承大統。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Tianli (1328), Wenzong entered to succeed to the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1328, Wenzong succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙即易服南迎，至於汴郊見焉。

translations.literal: Alihaiya immediately changed his garb and went south to welcome him, meeting him in the suburbs of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya at once changed his mourning dress and went south to welcome him, meeting the emperor in the suburbs of Bian.

sentences.zh: 帝命復鎮汴省。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him again to govern Henan province at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to resume governing Henan province from Bian.

sentences.zh: 時當艱難之際，阿禮海牙高價糴粟，以峙糧儲，命近郡分治戎器，閱士卒，括馬民間，以備不虞。

translations.literal: At a time of hardship, Alihaiya purchased grain at high prices to stockpile provisions, ordered nearby prefectures to prepare weapons separately, reviewed soldiers, and requisitioned horses among the people to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: In those difficult days Alihaiya bought grain at high prices to build up reserves, ordered neighboring prefectures to ready weapons, inspected the troops, and requisitioned horses from the populace against any emergency.

sentences.zh: 先是，文宗即位之詔已播告天下，而陝西官府結連靖安王等起兵，東擊潼關。

translations.literal: Earlier, the proclamation of Wenzong's accession had already been announced throughout the realm, yet the officials of Shaanxi joined with the Prince of Jing'an and others to raise troops and strike east against Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Although Wenzong's accession edict had already been proclaimed throughout the realm, the officials of Shaanxi allied with the Prince of Jing'an and others, raised troops, and marched east against Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙開府庫，量出鈔二十五萬緡，屬諸行省參政河南淮北蒙古軍都萬戶朶列圖、廉訪副使萬家閭犒軍河南以禦之。

translations.literal: Alihaiya opened the treasury, measured out two hundred fifty thousand strings of paper money, and entrusted Associate Grand Councillor of the Branch Secretariat Duoletu, Chief Commander of the Henan and North-of-the-Huai Mongol Army, and Vice Commissioner of Surveillance Wanjialü to reward the army in Henan and resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya opened the treasury, issued two hundred fifty thousand strings of paper money, and entrusted Duoletu, associate grand councillor of the branch secretariat and chief commander of the Henan and North-of-the-Huai Mongol army, together with Vice Commissioner of Surveillance Wanjialü, to reward the troops in Henan and hold the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 令都鎮撫卜伯率軍吏巡行南陽、高門、武關、荊子諸隘，南至襄、川二江之口，督以嚴備。

translations.literal: He ordered the Chief Pacification Commissioner Bubei to lead military officers on patrol through the passes of Nanyang, Gaomen, Wuguan, and Jingzi, south to the mouths of the Xiang and Chuan rivers, and urged strict preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Chief Pacification Commissioner Bubei to lead military officers on patrol through the passes at Nanyang, Gaomen, Wuguan, and Jingzi, as far south as the mouths of the Xiang and Chuan rivers, and pressed them to prepare strictly.

sentences.zh: 萬戶博羅守潼關，不能軍。

translations.literal: The chiliarch Boluo defended Tong Pass but could not hold the army together.
translations.idiomatic: The chiliarch Boluo held Tong Pass but failed to keep his command in order.

sentences.zh: 是月二十五日，只兒哈率小汪緫帥、脫帖木兒萬戶等之兵，突出潼關，東掠閿鄉，披靈寶，盪陝州、新安諸郡邑，放兵四劫，迤邐前進。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of that month, Zhierha led the troops of Commander-in-Chief Xiao Wang, the chiliarch Tuotiemuer, and others in a sudden breakout from Tong Pass, raiding east through Minxiang, breaking through Lingbao, and sweeping the prefectures and counties of Shanzhou, Xin'an, and others; they let their soldiers plunder on all sides and advanced in succession.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth of that month Zhierha led the forces of Commander-in-Chief Xiao Wang, the chiliarch Tuotiemuer, and others in a sudden breakout from Tong Pass, raiding east through Minxiang, breaking through Lingbao, and sweeping Shanzhou, Xin'an, and neighboring counties; his men looted everywhere as they pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 河南告急之使狎至，而朶列圖亦以兵寡為言。

translations.literal: Envoys from Henan reporting emergency arrived in close succession, and Duoletu also spoke of having too few troops.
translations.idiomatic: Emergency envoys from Henan arrived one after another, and Duoletu also reported that his forces were too few.

sentences.zh: 十月一日，阿禮海牙集省憲官屬，問以長策，無有言者。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month, Alihaiya assembled the provincial and surveillance officials and asked them for a long-term plan; no one spoke.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the tenth month Alihaiya assembled the provincial and surveillance officials and asked for a long-term plan, but no one had anything to say.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙曰：「汴在南北之交，使西人得至此，則江南三省之道不通于畿甸，軍旅應接何日息乎。

translations.literal: Alihaiya said: "Bian stands at the junction of north and south. If the western forces reach here, then the routes of the three southern provinces will no longer connect with the capital region—when would the strain of military response ever cease?
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya said: "Bian stands where north and south meet. If the western armies reach here, the routes from the three southern provinces to the capital will be cut, and when would the burden of military response ever end?

sentences.zh: 夫事有緩急輕重，今重莫如足兵，急莫如足食。

translations.literal: Affairs have degrees of urgency and importance; at present nothing is more important than having sufficient troops, and nothing more urgent than having sufficient food.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs differ in urgency and weight; at present nothing matters more than enough troops, and nothing is more urgent than enough food.

sentences.zh: 吾徵湖廣之平陽、保定兩翼軍，與吾省之鄧新翼、廬州、沂、郯砲弩手諸軍，以備虎牢；

translations.literal: I shall summon the Pingyang and Baoding wing armies of Huguang, together with the Dengxin Wing, Luzhou, Yi, and Tan catapult-and-crossbow corps of our province, to defend Hulao;
translations.idiomatic: I will summon the Pingyang and Baoding wing armies from Huguang, together with our province's Dengxin Wing and the catapult-and-crossbow corps of Luzhou, Yi, and Tan, to hold Hulao;

sentences.zh: 裕州哈剌魯、鄧州孫萬戶兩軍，以備武關、荊子口。

translations.literal: the two armies of Harlu at Yuzhou and Sun the chiliarch at Dengzhou, to defend Wuguan and Jingzikou.
translations.idiomatic: and the two armies of Harlu at Yuzhou and Sun the chiliarch at Dengzhou to hold Wuguan and Jingzikou.

sentences.zh: 以屬郡之兵及蒙古兩都萬戶、左右兩衛、諸部丁壯之可入軍者，給馬乘貲裝，立行伍，以次備諸隘。

translations.literal: With the troops of subordinate prefectures, the two capital chiliarchies of the Mongols, the Left and Right Guards, and able-bodied men of the various districts fit for service, I shall provide horses, travel expenses, and equipment, establish ranks, and in order man the various passes.
translations.idiomatic: With the troops of the subordinate prefectures, the two Mongol capital chiliarchies, the Left and Right Guards, and every able-bodied man fit for service, I will provide horses, supplies, and equipment, form them into ranks, and station them at the passes in turn.

sentences.zh: 芍陂等屯兵本自襄、鄧諸軍來田者，還其軍，益以民之丁壯，使守襄陽、白土、峽州諸隘。

translations.literal: The garrison troops at Shaobo and elsewhere originally came from the Xiang and Deng armies to farm the fields; I shall return them to their armies and supplement them with civilian able-bodied men to guard the passes of Xiangyang, Baitu, and Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison troops at Shaobo and elsewhere were originally drawn from the Xiang and Deng armies to farm the fields; I will return them to their units, add civilian recruits, and use them to hold the passes at Xiangyang, Baitu, and Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 別遣塔海以備自蜀至者，以汴、汝、荊、襄、兩淮之馬以給之，府庫不足，則命郡縣假諸殷富之家。

translations.literal: I shall separately dispatch Tahai to guard against those coming from Shu, supplying him with horses from Bian, Ru, Jing, Xiang, and the Two Huai; if the treasury is insufficient, I shall order the prefectures and counties to borrow from wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: I will send Tahai separately to guard against any force coming from Shu, supply him with horses from Bian, Ru, Jing, Xiang, and the Two Huai, and if the treasury falls short, order the prefectures and counties to borrow from wealthy families.

sentences.zh: 安豐等郡之粟，溯黃河運至于陝，糴諸汴、汝，近郡者，則運諸滎陽以達於虎牢。

translations.literal: The grain of Anfeng and other prefectures shall be transported upstream along the Yellow River to Shan; grain shall be purchased at Bian and Ru, and from nearby prefectures it shall be transported to Xingyang to reach Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from Anfeng and other prefectures will be shipped up the Yellow River to Shan; grain will be bought at Bian and Ru, and from nearby prefectures it will be sent to Xingyang and on to Hulao.

sentences.zh: 吾與諸軍各奮忠義以從王事，宜無不濟者。」

translations.literal: If I and the various armies each exert loyalty and righteousness in serving the royal cause, there should be nothing that cannot succeed."
translations.idiomatic: If the armies and I each devote ourselves loyally to the royal cause, there is nothing we should not accomplish."

sentences.zh: 衆曰：「唯。」

translations.literal: The assembly said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: The assembly answered: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 命即日部分行事。

translations.literal: He ordered that the assignments be carried out that very day.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the assignments carried out that same day.

sentences.zh: 自伯顏不花王以下省都事李元德等，凡省之屬吏與有官而家居者，各授以事而出。

translations.literal: From Prince Bayanbuhua down to the provincial secretary Li Yuande and others, all subordinate clerks of the province and those with office who were living at home were each given duties and sent out.
translations.idiomatic: From Prince Bayanbuhua down to the provincial secretary Li Yuande and the rest, every subordinate clerk of the province and every official living at home was given a task and sent out.

sentences.zh: 廉訪使董守中、僉事沙沙在南陽，右丞脫帖木兒、廉訪使卜顏在虎牢，分遣兵馬以聽其調用。

translations.literal: Surveillance Commissioner Dong Shouzhong and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Shasha were at Nanyang; Right Vice Councillor Tuotiemuer and Surveillance Commissioner Buyan were at Hulao; troops and horses were dispatched separately for their use.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Dong Shouzhong and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Shasha were at Nanyang, while Right Vice Councillor Tuotiemuer and Surveillance Commissioner Buyan were at Hulao; he dispatched troops and horses to each so they could be called up as needed.

sentences.zh: 餽餉之行，千車相望，阿禮海牙親閱實之，必豐必良，信以期會。

translations.literal: Supply convoys went out, a thousand carts in sight of one another; Alihaiya personally inspected and verified them, ensuring they were ample and good, and trusted to meet the deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: Supply convoys rolled out by the thousand; Alihaiya personally inspected each shipment to ensure it was ample and sound, and saw that every deadline was kept.

sentences.zh: 自虎牢之南至於襄、漢，無不畢給。

translations.literal: From south of Hulao to Xiang and Han, nothing failed to be fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: From south of Hulao to the Xiang and Han regions, every need was fully met.

sentences.zh: 蓋為粟二十萬石，豆如之，兵甲五十五萬，芻萬萬。

translations.literal: In all there were two hundred thousand shi of grain, the same amount of beans, five hundred fifty thousand sets of armor and weapons, and fodder numbering one hundred million.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were two hundred thousand shi of grain, as much again in beans, five hundred fifty thousand sets of arms and armor, and fodder numbering one hundred million.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝廷置行樞密院以緫西事。

translations.literal: At this time the court established a Branch Bureau of Military Affairs to oversee western affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the court established a branch bureau of military affairs to oversee the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 襄、漢、荊湖、河南郡縣皆缺官，阿禮海牙便宜擇材以處之，朝廷皆從其請。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties of Xiang, Han, Jinghu, and Henan all lacked officials; Alihaiya at his discretion selected talent to fill the posts, and the court approved all his requests.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties throughout Xiang, Han, Jinghu, and Henan were without officials; Alihaiya selected men of talent at his discretion to fill the posts, and the court approved every request.

sentences.zh: 是月，西兵逼河南，行院使來報，曰：「西人北行者度河中以趨懷、孟、磁；

translations.literal: That month, as western troops pressed upon Henan, the commissioner of the branch bureau came to report, saying: "Those westerners going north cross the Yellow River to advance on Huai, Meng, and Ci;
translations.idiomatic: That month, as western troops pressed on Henan, the branch bureau commissioner reported: "The northerly western force is crossing the Yellow River toward Huai, Meng, and Ci;

sentences.zh: 南行者帖木哥，過武關，掠鄧州而殘之，直趨襄陽，攻破郡邑三十餘，橫絕數千里，所過殺官吏，焚廬舍，虜民人婦女財物，賊虐殄盡，西結囊家469f以蜀兵至矣。」

translations.literal: the southerly one, Timur-gh, passed Wuguan, plundered Dengzhou and ravaged it, and pressed straight toward Xiangyang; he broke more than thirty prefectures and counties, cutting off thousands of li; wherever he passed he killed officials, burned dwellings, and carried off the people, women, and goods; the bandits exhausted all with cruelty; in the west he allied with the Nangjia'er faction, declaring that Shu troops had arrived."
translations.idiomatic: the southerly force under Timur-gh has passed Wuguan, sacked Dengzhou, and is driving straight on Xiangyang; it has overrun more than thirty prefectures and counties and cut a swath thousands of li wide, killing officials, burning homes, and seizing people, women, and goods wherever it goes; the rebels have ravaged everything in their path, and in the west they have allied with the Nangjia'er faction, declaring that Shu troops are already on the march."

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙益督餉西行，遣行院官塔海領兵攻帖木哥，而又設備於江、黃，置鐵繩於峽口，作舟艦以待戰。

translations.literal: Alihaiya further urged supplies westward, dispatched the branch bureau official Tahai to lead troops against Timur-gh, and also made preparations along the Yangzi and Yellow rivers, set iron chains at the gorge mouths, and built warships awaiting battle.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya pressed supplies westward still harder, sent the branch bureau official Tahai to lead troops against Timur-gh, and also made ready along the Yangzi and Yellow rivers, set iron chains at the gorge mouths, and built warships for battle.

sentences.zh: 十九日，師與西兵遇於鞏縣之石渡，而湖廣所徵太原之兵最為可用。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day the army met the western troops at Shidu in Gong county, and among the troops summoned from Taiyuan by Huguang those were the most usable.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth the army met the western force at Shidu in Gong county; of all the troops summoned from Taiyuan by Huguang, these proved the most reliable.

sentences.zh: 甫至，未及食，或趣之倍道以進，轉戰及暮，兩軍殺傷與墮澗谷死者相等，而虎牢遂為敵有。

translations.literal: They had just arrived and had not yet eaten when some urged them to advance by double marches; fighting continued until evening, and the killed and wounded on both sides, together with those who fell into ravines and gullies, were equal in number, and Hulao was then lost to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: They had just arrived and not yet eaten when someone pressed them to march at double speed; the fighting lasted until evening, casualties on both sides were equal, many men fell into ravines and gullies, and Hulao fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 兵儲巨萬，阿禮海牙盡其心、民殫其力者，一旦悉亡焉。

translations.literal: Military stores numbered in the tens of thousands; what Alihaiya had exhausted his heart over and what the people had exhausted their strength for were all lost in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Stores worth a fortune—everything Alihaiya had poured his heart into and the people had strained every nerve to gather—were lost in a single day.

sentences.zh: 行省院與諸軍斂兵退。

translations.literal: The branch secretariat and bureau and the various armies gathered their troops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat, the branch bureau, and the various armies gathered their forces and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 二十二日至汴，民大恐。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day they reached Bian, and the people were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second they reached Bian, and the people were terrified.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙前後遣使告于朝，輒為也先捏留不遣，不得朝廷音問已二十日，阿禮海牙亦憂之，親出行撫其民。

translations.literal: Alihaiya repeatedly sent envoys to report to court, but they were detained and not dispatched by Yeshannie; for twenty days he received no word from court, and Alihaiya was also troubled by this; he personally went out to reassure the people.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya sent envoys to court again and again, but Yeshannie detained them and would not let them through; for twenty days he had no word from the capital, and Alihaiya, deeply worried, went out himself to reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 乃修城闕以備衝突，立四門以通往來，戒卒伍以嚴守衛。

translations.literal: He then repaired the city walls and towers to guard against assault, opened the four gates to allow passage back and forth, and admonished the soldiers to maintain strict defense.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the walls and towers against assault, kept the four gates open for traffic, and admonished the garrison to maintain strict guard.

sentences.zh: 時雖甚危急，阿禮海牙朝夕出入，聲色不動，怡然如平時，衆賴以安。

translations.literal: Although the time was extremely perilous, Alihaiya went in and out morning and evening without change in voice or countenance, easy and composed as in ordinary times, and the people relied on this to be reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Though the crisis was extreme, Alihaiya came and went morning and evening with unchanged voice and expression, as calm as in ordinary times, and the people took heart from him.

sentences.zh: 十一月六日，西師逼城將百里而近，阿禮海牙召行院將帥、憲司與凡在官者，而告之曰：「吾荷國厚恩，唯有一死以報上耳。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the eleventh month, as the western army pressed upon the city to within about a hundred li, Alihaiya summoned the generals of the branch bureau, the surveillance officials, and all who held office, and told them: "I have received the state's deep grace; I have only death with which to repay my sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the eleventh month, with the western army within a hundred li of the city, Alihaiya summoned the branch bureau commanders, the surveillance officials, and every officer on duty and said: "I owe the state a deep debt of gratitude; I have nothing to offer but my life in the emperor's service.

sentences.zh: 行院之出，唯敵是圖，而退保吾城，不亦怯乎？

translations.literal: When the branch bureau went out, it sought only the enemy; yet to withdraw and hold only our city—is that not cowardice?
translations.idiomatic: The branch bureau went out to seek the enemy alone; to withdraw and merely hold our city—is that not cowardice?

sentences.zh: 然敵亦烏合之衆，何所受命而敢犯我乎？

translations.literal: Yet the enemy too are a mob gathered together; from whom do they receive orders that they dare invade us?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the enemy too are a mob; from whom do they take orders that they dare invade us?

sentences.zh: 且吾甲兵非不堅勁，芻峙非不豐給，而弗利者，太平日久，將校不知兵，吏士不練習，彼所以得披猖至此。

translations.literal: Moreover, our armor and weapons are not unstrong, and our stored fodder is not unabundant; what has not benefited us is that peace has lasted long, officers do not know warfare, and clerks and soldiers are untrained—that is why the enemy has been able to rampage this far.
translations.idiomatic: Our armor is strong and our fodder ample; what has failed us is that after long peace our officers no longer know war and our clerks and soldiers are untrained—that is why the enemy has been able to rampage this far.

sentences.zh: 彼誠知我聖天子之命，則衆沮而散爾，何足慮乎。

translations.literal: If they truly knew the command of our sage Son of Heaven, then the multitude would be discouraged and would disperse—what is there to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: If they truly understood the command of our sage emperor, their ranks would lose heart and scatter—what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 吾今遣使告于朝，請降詔大赦脅從詿誤。

translations.literal: I now send envoys to report to court and request an edict of general amnesty for those coerced and misled into following.
translations.idiomatic: I will send envoys to court now and ask for an edict of general amnesty for those coerced or misled into following the rebels.

sentences.zh: 比詔下，先募士，以即位詔及朝廷招諭之文入其軍，明示利害。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrives, I shall first recruit men to carry the accession proclamation and the court's summons into their army and clearly show them the gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrives, I will first recruit men to carry the accession proclamation and the court's summons into the enemy camp and make the stakes plain.

sentences.zh: 吾整大軍西嚮以征之，別遣驍將率精騎數千上龍門，繞出其後，使之進無所投，退無所歸，成擒於鞏、洛之間必矣。

translations.literal: I shall marshal a great army westward to campaign against them, and separately dispatch a fierce general to lead several thousand elite cavalry up Longmen and circle behind them, so that advancing they have nowhere to go and retreating they have nowhere to return—they will surely be captured between Gong and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: I will marshal a great army and march west against them, and send a fierce general with several thousand elite cavalry up Longmen to circle behind them, so that advancing they have nowhere to go and retreating nowhere to return—they will surely be taken between Gong and Luo.

sentences.zh: 而我軍所獲陝西官吏，命有司羈而食之，一無所戮。」

translations.literal: As for the Shaanxi officials captured by our army, I order the responsible offices to detain and feed them, and not execute a single one."
translations.idiomatic: As for the Shaanxi officials our army captures, I order the responsible offices to detain and provision them, and not execute a single one."

sentences.zh: 衆曰：「諾，唯命。」

translations.literal: The assembly said: "Yes—we await your command."
translations.idiomatic: The assembly answered: "Yes—we await your orders."

sentences.zh: 即日與行院整兵南薰門外以行。

translations.literal: That same day he and the branch bureau marshaled troops outside the Nanxun Gate and set out.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he and the branch bureau marshaled their troops outside the Nanxun Gate and set out.

sentences.zh: 會有使者自京師還，言齊王已克上都，奉天子寶璽來歸，刻日至京矣。

translations.literal: Just then an envoy returned from the capital, saying that the Prince of Qi had already taken Shangdu and was bringing the Son of Heaven's imperial seal back in submission, and would reach the capital within the day.
translations.idiomatic: Just then an envoy returned from the capital reporting that the Prince of Qi had taken Shangdu and was bringing the imperial seal back in submission, and would reach the capital within the day.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙乃置酒高會於省堂以賀，發書告屬郡，報諸江南三省，而募士得蘭住者齎書諭之。

translations.literal: Alihaiya then set out wine for a grand gathering in the provincial hall to celebrate, sent letters to inform the subordinate prefectures, reported to the three southern provinces, and recruited a man named Lanzhu to carry the proclamation and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya then held a grand feast in the provincial hall to celebrate, sent letters to the subordinate prefectures, notified the three southern provinces, and recruited a man named Lanzhu to carry the proclamation to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 西人猶搒掠蘭住，訊以其實，而朝廷亦遣都護月魯帖木兒從十餘人奉詔放散西軍之在虎牢者。

translations.literal: The westerners still beat and plundered Lanzhu and interrogated him for the truth, while the court also dispatched the Chief Guardian Yuelü Timur with more than ten followers bearing an edict to disband the western army at Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: The westerners still beat and robbed Lanzhu and interrogated him to learn the truth, while the court also sent Chief Guardian Yuelü Timur with more than ten followers bearing an edict to disband the western army at Hulao.

sentences.zh: 西人殺其從者之半，械都護以送諸荊王所。

translations.literal: The westerners killed half his followers, put the Chief Guardian in fetters, and sent him to the Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The westerners killed half his followers, put the chief guardian in fetters, and sent him to the Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 荊王時在河南之白馬寺，以是西人雖未解散，各已駭悟。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jing was then at White Horse Temple in Henan; because of this, although the westerners had not yet dispersed, each was already shaken and awakened.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jing was then at White Horse Temple in Henan; because of this, though the westerners had not yet dispersed, each man was already shaken into awareness.

sentences.zh: 又聞行省院以兵至，猶豫不敢進。

translations.literal: They also heard that the branch secretariat and bureau were coming with troops, and hesitated, not daring to advance.
translations.idiomatic: When they also heard that the branch secretariat and bureau were marching with troops, they hesitated and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又使參政馮不花親諭之，乃信服。

translations.literal: The court further sent Associate Grand Councillor Feng Buhua to instruct them in person, and then they believed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent Associate Grand Councillor Feng Buhua to instruct them in person, and they submitted in good faith.

sentences.zh: 靖安王遣使四輩與蘭住來請命，逡巡而去，難平。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jing'an sent four envoys together with Lanzhu to come and request orders; they lingered and departed, and pacification was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jing'an sent four envoys together with Lanzhu to seek orders; they lingered and withdrew, and pacification remained difficult.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙乃解嚴報捷，斂餘財以還民，從陝西求民人之被俘掠者歸其家，凡數千人。

translations.literal: Alihaiya then lifted the emergency measures and reported victory, gathered surplus funds to return to the people, and from Shaanxi sought the common people who had been captured and plundered to restore them to their families—in all several thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya then lifted the emergency measures and reported victory, returned surplus funds to the people, and from Shaanxi recovered the common people who had been captured and plundered and sent them home—several thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 陝西官吏被獲者，皆遣還其所。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi officials who had been captured were all sent back to their places.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi officials who had been captured were all sent back to their posts.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙自始至鎮，迨乎告功，居汴省者數月。

translations.literal: From the time Alihaiya first arrived to govern until he reported success, he resided at Henan province in Bian for several months.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Alihaiya first took up his post until he reported victory, he governed Henan from Bian for several months.

sentences.zh: 後以功遷陝西行御史大夫，復拜中書省平章政事。

translations.literal: Later, for his merit he was transferred to Grand Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and again appointed Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his service he was made grand censor of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate and again appointed grand councillor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁字太初，回回氏。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding, courtesy name Taichu, was of the Huihui clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding, whose courtesy name was Taichu, was of Huihui descent.

sentences.zh: 父亦速馬因，仕至大都南北兩城兵馬都指揮使。

translations.literal: His father Yisumayin served to the post of Chief Commander of Military Affairs for the North and South Cities of the Great Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yisumayin rose to chief commander of military affairs for the north and south cities of the Great Capital.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁幼穎悟嗜學，所讀書一過目即終身不忘。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding from youth was sharp and intelligent and loved learning; whatever book he read, once he glanced at it he never forgot it for life.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yihediyaerding was bright and devoted to learning; whatever he read once, he remembered for life.

sentences.zh: 尤工其國字語。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in the script and language of his country.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in his people's script and language.

sentences.zh: 初為中書掾，以年勞授江西行省員外郎，入為吏部主事，不再閱月，固辭。

translations.literal: At first he served as a clerk of the Central Secretariat; for years of service he was appointed Outer Section Officer of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, entered service as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, and within less than a month firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk in the Central Secretariat and, for years of service, was appointed outer section officer of the Jiangxi branch secretariat; he entered the Ministry of Personnel as a principal clerk, but within a month firmly declined the post.

sentences.zh: 擢刑部員外郎，四方所上獄，反復披閱成牘，多所平反。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Outer Section Officer of the Ministry of Justice; for cases submitted from the four directions he repeatedly examined the completed dossiers and reversed many wrongful verdicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to outer section officer of the Ministry of Justice; for cases submitted from every quarter he carefully reviewed the completed dossiers and reversed many wrongful verdicts.

sentences.zh: 遷陝西漢中道肅政廉訪司僉事，不赴。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of the Shaanxi Hanzhong Circuit Commission for Rectifying Governance and Promoting Integrity, but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant surveillance commissioner on the Shaanxi Hanzhong circuit, but did not take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 改中書右司員外郎，尋陞郎中。

translations.literal: He was changed to Outer Section Officer of the Right Department of the Central Secretariat, and before long was promoted to Department Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as outer section officer of the right department of the Central Secretariat and soon promoted to department director.

sentences.zh: 一日，與同列共議獄，有異其說者，奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「公等讀律，苟不能變通以適事宜，譬之醫者，雖熟於方論，而不能切脈用藥，則於疾痛奚益哉。」

translations.literal: One day, while deliberating a case together with his colleagues, when someone differed from his view, Yihediyaerding said: "You gentlemen read the law; if you cannot adapt flexibly to suit the circumstances, it is like a physician who, though well versed in prescriptions and treatises, cannot feel the pulse and apply medicine—what good would that do for illness and pain?"
translations.idiomatic: One day, while deliberating a case with his colleagues, someone took a different view, and Yihediyaerding said: "You read the law, but if you cannot adapt it to fit the circumstances, you are like a physician who knows every prescription by heart yet cannot feel the pulse and prescribe—what good does that do the patient?"

sentences.zh: 同列雖不平，識者服其為名言。

translations.literal: His colleagues were displeased, but those with discernment admired his words as a fine saying.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues were displeased, but discerning men admired the remark as a fine saying.

sentences.zh: 大德八年肆赦，廷議惟官吏因事受賕者不預。
