translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade (1304), a general amnesty was proclaimed; at court it was proposed that only officials who had accepted bribes in the course of official business be excluded.
translations.idiomatic: In 1304 a general amnesty was proclaimed, and at court it was proposed that officials who had taken bribes in the course of duty should be excluded.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding said: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding said: "That will not do.

sentences.zh: 恩如雨露，萬物均被，贓吏固可嫉，比之盜賊則有間矣。

translations.literal: Grace is like rain and dew—all things equally receive it. Corrupt officials may indeed be detestable, but compared with robbers and bandits there is a difference.
translations.idiomatic: Grace is like rain and dew—it should fall on all alike. Corrupt officials are indeed contemptible, but they are not the same as robbers and bandits.

sentences.zh: 宥盜而不宥吏，何耶？」

translations.literal: To pardon robbers but not pardon officials—why is that?"
translations.idiomatic: To pardon robbers but not officials—why should that be?"

sentences.zh: 刑部嘗有獄事，上讞既論決，已而丞相知其失，以譴右司主者。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice once had a criminal case; the memorial for imperial decision had already been adjudicated, but later the chief councillor learned of the error and rebuked the head of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice once handled a criminal case whose memorial for imperial decision had already been settled; when the chief councillor later discovered the error, he censured the head of the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁初未嘗署其案，因取成案閱之，竊署其名於下。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding had never signed that dossier at first; he therefore took the completed file to read it and secretly signed his name beneath.
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding had never signed that dossier in the first place; he took the completed file, read it through, and quietly added his name at the bottom.

sentences.zh: 或訝之曰：「茲獄之失，公實不與，丞相方譴怒而公反追署其案，何也？」

translations.literal: Someone expressed surprise and said: "In the error of this case you were not actually involved; the chief councillor is just now rebuking in anger, yet you go back and sign the dossier—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked in astonishment: "You had no part in this case's error; the chief councillor is angry and censuring others—why would you go back and sign the dossier now?"

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「吾偶不署此案耳，豈有與諸君同事而獨幸免哉。」

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding said: "I happened not to sign this case—that is all; how could I work together with you gentlemen and alone escape unscathed?"
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding replied: "I simply failed to sign this case—how could I serve alongside you and alone escape blame?"

sentences.zh: 丞相聞而賢之，同列因以獲免。

translations.literal: When the chief councillor heard of it he regarded him as worthy, and his colleagues were thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief councillor heard this he admired him, and his colleagues were spared as a result.

sentences.zh: 遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 時左司闕一都事，平章梁暗都剌謂奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「人之材幹固嘗有之，惟篤實不欺為難得，公當以所知舉。」

translations.literal: At the time the Left Department lacked one secretariat supervisor; Grand Councillor Liang Andula said to Yihediyaerding: "Men's talent and capacity are common enough; only steadfast honesty without deception is hard to find—you should recommend those you know."
translations.idiomatic: The Left Department then lacked a secretariat supervisor; Grand Councillor Liang Andula told Yihediyaerding: "Talent is common enough, but steadfast honesty is rare—you should recommend someone you know."

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁遂以王毅、李迪為言，一時輿論莫不稱允。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding thereupon proposed Wang Yi and Li Di, and public opinion at the time unanimously approved.
translations.idiomatic: He nominated Wang Yi and Li Di, and public opinion at once approved.

sentences.zh: 又嘗論朝士，如王仁卿、賈元播、高彥敬、敬威卿、李清臣輩可大用，時諸公處下僚，後皆如其言。

translations.literal: He also once discussed court officials, saying that men such as Wang Renqing, Jia Yuanbo, Gao Yanjing, Jing Weiqing, and Li Qingchen could be greatly employed; at the time those gentlemen held lower posts, and later events proved his words true.
translations.idiomatic: He also once remarked that court officials such as Wang Renqing, Jia Yuanbo, Gao Yanjing, Jing Weiqing, and Li Qingchen were fit for high office; they were then in junior posts, and later events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林侍講學士、知制誥兼修國史，轉中奉大夫、集賢大學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician Lecturer, Drafter of Imperial Proclamations, and Compiler of the National History, then advanced to Grand Master of Proper Service and Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin academician lecturer, drafter of imperial proclamations, and compiler of the national history, then advanced to Grand Master of Proper Service and grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除江東建康道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed surveillance commissioner of the Jiandong Jiankang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made surveillance commissioner of the Jiandong Jiankang circuit.

sentences.zh: 始視事，見以獄具陳列庭下甚備，問之，乃前官創製以待有罪者。

translations.literal: When he first took up his duties he saw torture implements arrayed very completely in the courtyard below; on inquiry, these had been devised by a former official to await the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: On first taking office he found torture implements laid out in full array in the courtyard; inquiry showed a predecessor had devised them for use on the condemned.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁蹙然曰：「凡逮至臬司，皆命官及有出身之吏，廉得其情，則將服罪，獄具毋庸施也。」

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding said with a troubled look: "Whenever cases reach the provincial judicial office, they are all officials by appointment and clerks with formal credentials; once the facts are fairly established they will confess—there is no need to apply torture implements."
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding said with a troubled expression: "Cases that reach this office involve appointed officials and credentialed clerks; once the facts are fairly established they will confess—torture implements are unnecessary."

sentences.zh: 即屏去之。

translations.literal: He immediately had them removed.
translations.idiomatic: He had them removed at once.

sentences.zh: 監憲一年，贓吏削跡。

translations.literal: After one year of censorial oversight, corrupt officials vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: After a year in the surveillance post, corrupt officials had all but disappeared.

sentences.zh: 至大初元，立尚書省，拜參議尚書省事，召至京師，懇辭不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhida reign the Department of State Affairs was established; he was appointed counsellor of the Department of State Affairs, summoned to the capital, and earnestly declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhida reign a Department of State Affairs was established; he was appointed counsellor of the Department of State Affairs and summoned to the capital, but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 改立中書省，復拜參議中書省事，亦以疾辭。

translations.literal: When the Central Secretariat was restored he was again appointed associate minister of Central Secretariat affairs, and again declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Central Secretariat was restored he was again offered the associate ministership, and again declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年卒，年四十有七。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yanyou (1314), at the age of forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1314, at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 脫烈海牙

translations.literal: Tuoliehaiya
translations.idiomatic: Tuoliehaiya

sentences.zh: 脫烈海牙，畏吾氏。

translations.literal: Tuoliehaiya was of the Uyghur clan.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoliehaiya was of Uyghur descent.

sentences.zh: 世居別失拔里之地。

translations.literal: For generations his family dwelt in the land of Bieshibali.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived for generations in Bieshibali.

sentences.zh: 曾祖闊華八撒朮，當太祖西征，導其主亦都護迎降。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kuohuabaszhu, when Taizu campaigned westward, guided his lord Idiqut in coming forward to submit.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kuohuabaszhu, when Taizu marched west, guided his lord the Idiqut in surrendering to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其有識，欲官之，辭以不敏。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his discernment and wished to give him office, but he declined on grounds of incompetence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his foresight and wished to appoint him, but he declined on grounds of unworthiness.

sentences.zh: 祖八剌朮，始徙真定，仕至帥府鎮撫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Balazhu first moved to Zhending and rose in office to pacification commissioner of the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Balazhu first settled in Zhending and rose to pacification commissioner of the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 富而樂施，或貸不償，則火其券，人稱為長者。

translations.literal: He was wealthy and delighted in giving; when loans went unpaid he burned the bonds, and people called him a man of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy and generous, he would burn unpaid loan bonds, and people called him a man of true stature.

sentences.zh: 父闍里赤，性純正，知讀書。

translations.literal: His father Zhanlizhi was upright in character and knew how to read books.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhanlizhi was upright by nature and literate.

sentences.zh: 脫烈海牙幼嗜學，警敏絕人。

translations.literal: Tuoliehaiya from youth loved learning and was alert and quick beyond others.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tuoliehaiya loved learning and was exceptionally quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 性整暇，雖居倉卒，未嘗見其急遽。

translations.literal: His nature was composed and unhurried; even in sudden crises he was never seen flustered.
translations.idiomatic: Composed by temperament, he was never seen flustered even in sudden crises.

sentences.zh: 喜從文士游，犬馬聲色之娛，一無所好。

translations.literal: He delighted in associating with literary men and had no taste whatsoever for diversions of horses, dogs, music, or women.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed the company of scholars and cared nothing for horses, hounds, music, or courtesans.

sentences.zh: 由中書宣使，出為寧晉主簿。

translations.literal: Starting as a Central Secretariat dispatch clerk, he went out to serve as registrar of Ningjin.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning as a Central Secretariat dispatch clerk, he was posted as registrar of Ningjin.

sentences.zh: 改隆平縣達魯花赤，均賦興學，劭農平訟，橋梁、水防、備荒之政，無一不舉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be darughachi of Longping county, where he equalized tax levies, promoted schools, encouraged agriculture and settled lawsuits, and carried out every policy for bridges, flood control, and famine preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to serve as darughachi of Longping county, he equalized taxes, promoted schools, encouraged farming and settled disputes, and carried through every measure for bridges, flood control, and famine relief.

sentences.zh: 及滿去，民勒石以紀其政。

translations.literal: When his term ended the people carved a stone to record his administration.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended the people set up a stone to commemorate his administration.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時江西胡參政殺其弟，訟久不決，脫烈海牙一訊竟伏其辜。

translations.literal: At the time Hu, the regional administrator of Jiangxi, had killed his younger brother; the lawsuit long went unresolved, but Tuoliehaiya with one interrogation brought the crime to light.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu, regional administrator of Jiangxi, had killed his younger brother and the case dragged on unresolved, Tuoliehaiya settled it in a single hearing and established his guilt.

sentences.zh: 出僉燕南道肅政廉訪司事，務存大體，不事苛察。

translations.literal: He went out as assistant surveillance commissioner of the Yannan circuit, aiming to preserve the broad principles and not engage in harsh scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as assistant surveillance commissioner of the Yannan circuit, he upheld broad principles and avoided petty scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 在任六年，黜污吏百四十有奇。

translations.literal: During six years in office he dismissed more than a hundred and forty corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: In six years of service he removed more than a hundred and forty corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部郎中，轉右司員外郎，陞右司郎中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as director in the Ministry of Revenue, transferred to vice-director of the Right Department, and promoted to director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director in the Ministry of Revenue, then vice-director and director of the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 贊畫之力居多。

translations.literal: His contribution to planning and counsel was the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: He bore the greater part of the work in planning and counsel.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，知其嗜學，出祕府經籍及聖賢圖像以賜，時人榮之。

translations.literal: When Renzong was in the Eastern Palace he knew his love of learning and presented him with classics from the secret repository and images of sages and worthies; people of the time regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: While Renzong was heir apparent he knew Tuoliehaiya's love of learning and gave him classics from the imperial library and portraits of sages; contemporaries counted it a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 母霍氏卒，哀毀骨立，事聞，賜鈔五萬貫，給葬事。

translations.literal: When his mother, Lady Huo, died he mourned until he was skin and bone; the matter was reported, and he was granted fifty thousand strings of paper money for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother Lady Huo died he mourned until he was wasted to the bone; on report of this the court granted fifty thousand strings of paper money for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 起為吏部尚書，量能敘爵，以平允稱。

translations.literal: Recalled to serve as Minister of Personnel, he assigned ranks according to capacity and was known for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Minister of Personnel, he assigned ranks according to merit and was known for evenhanded fairness.

sentences.zh: 改禮部尚書，領會同館事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites and put in charge of the Hall of Mutual Accord.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Rites and placed in charge of the Hall of Mutual Accord.

sentences.zh: 進中奉大夫、荊湖北道宣慰使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master of Proper Service and pacification commissioner of the Jinghu North circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Proper Service and pacification commissioner of the Jinghu North circuit.

sentences.zh: 適峽人艱食，脫烈海牙先發廩賑之，而後以聞。

translations.literal: Just then the people of the gorges were short of food; Tuoliehaiya first opened the granaries to relieve them and only afterward reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When the gorge districts faced famine he opened the granaries to relieve them first and reported afterward.

sentences.zh: 朝議韙之。

translations.literal: Court discussion approved his action.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his action.

sentences.zh: 至治三年，遷淮東宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizhi (1323) he was transferred to pacification commissioner of Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1323 he was transferred to pacification commissioner of Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 七月，以疾卒于廣陵，年六十有七，贈通奉大夫、河南江北等處行中書省參知政事、護軍，追封恒山郡公。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died of illness at Guangling, aged sixty-seven; he was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Imperial Favor, Associate Grand Councillor of the Henan and Jiangbei Branch Secretariat, and Guardian of the Army, and enfeoffed as Duke of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he died of illness at Guangling at sixty-seven; he was posthumously made Grand Master of the Imperial Favor, associate grand councillor of the Henan and Jiangbei Branch Secretariat, and Guardian of the Army, and enfeoffed as Duke of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 弟觀音奴，廉明材幹，亦仕至清顯云。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guanyinnu was incorrupt, clear-sighted, and capable, and likewise rose to a pure and eminent office, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Guanyinnu was incorrupt and capable and likewise rose to a distinguished office, it is said.
